entries.test: Whether Sora's published samples and OpenAI's February 2024 technical report showed it failing to model basic physics consistently.
entries.note: This is a premise he asserts inside a rhetorical question. OpenAI itself acknowledged physics failures at launch.

entries.test: Reports of ChatGPT producing gibberish on 20 February 2024, and whether a cause had been given by the time of the post.
entries.note: The drafter added 'February 2024', which his words don't state, although context supports it. OpenAI posted an explanation on 21 February, which bears on 'unexplained'.

entries.test: Whether Gemini gave a wrong answer about the Apollo 11 crew in documented outputs from February 2024.
entries.note: He refers to a specific failure. 'Cannot reliably' turns this into a broader claim about general capability.

entries.test: Whether any formal verification or correctness guarantee existed for LLM-based systems as of February 2024.
entries.note: The drafter added an explicit conclusion that '$7 trillion is unjustified'. He only implies this through sarcasm.

entries.test: Whether Marcus's earliest public writing on LLMs (e.g. about GPT-2 in 2019) called them overhyped or oversold.
entries.note: The claim is about his own track record, not the bare statement 'LLMs are oversold'. The bare version would have no plain reading.
